archetype.name: Rebuilding
archetype.definition: A team still near the bottom of the league in shot and chance share for a third straight season, whose record reflects how often it is outplayed, not bad luck.

report.headline: Same bottom-three process, a hot week of finishing, and no real change yet
report.take:
Chicago is 8-14-2, sitting 31st of 32 on the site and last in the Central, and the record is an honest one. Its Pts vs Goal Diff of 0.6 is mid-pack, so it is neither stealing nor bleeding points in close games. The goal margin tells the story: -1.33 a game, 31st, built on an offense ranked 27th and a defense ranked 31st. At 5-on-5 it controls 0.425 of the expected goals and 0.45 of the shot attempts, 31st and 30th, against a league average of 0.5 on both.

What stands out is how little has changed. The xGF % was 0.431 two seasons ago and 0.424 last season; this year's 0.425 sits right between them. Last year's 72 standings points looked like modest progress, but the current pace projects to 62, which is back near the 61 of 2024-25. Whatever the rebuild is producing, it has not yet shown up in who has the puck or who gets the dangerous looks.

The numbers do hide two things. First, the team has been unlucky on the percentages. Its all-situations PDO is 96.6 against a league mean of 98.9, and the skaters are shooting 8.7% against a league 9.8%, so some of the goals-for gap should close on its own. Second, the goaltending damage is concentrated. Of the team's -9.1 GSAx, Arvid Soderblom accounts for -6.1 in just four starts. Spencer Knight, who has made 19 starts, sits at -1.9 with a .888 save %, below average but not a disaster. Neither of these turns the team into a playoff club. Together they explain why the scorelines have been even uglier than the underlying play.

The last five games (3-1-1, 4.4 goals a game) are the best stretch of the season, but two of the three wins came in overtime, and the last 10 are still -10 in goals. Treat it as percentages swinging back toward normal rather than a new team. Under Jeff Blashill this group is heading for a third straight bottom-three finish unless the shot share moves, and so far there is no sign that it will.

strengths.title: Special teams hold the line
strengths.body: The penalty kill runs at 79.5%, 14th and above the league's 77.2%, and the power play is mid-pack at 21.7%. The kill was also strong last season at 83.6%, so this looks like a repeatable skill rather than a hot month. It is the one phase where Chicago is not being outplayed.

strengths.title: Scoring has woken up lately
strengths.body: After 2.23 goals a game in October, Chicago scored 3.3 in November and 4.4 over the last five, including six-goal nights against Toronto and Vancouver. Part of that is shooting luck returning toward normal: the team's season shooting % of 8.7% still trails the league. Some of the uptick should stick, but not at last week's rate.

concerns.title: Out-chanced again, as every year
concerns.body: An xGF % of 0.425 ranks 31st, and it almost exactly matches the previous two seasons. The team also allows 29.3 shots on goal a game, 28th. This is the root of the record, and because it has held for three seasons, it is structural and not a slump.

concerns.title: Backup starts have been ruinous
concerns.body: The goalies together save .879, well below the league's .891. Soderblom's .842 and -6.1 GSAx in four starts drive most of that. Knight is closer to average, but at -1.9 GSAx he is not making up for the volume of shots. Fewer Soderblom starts would help, but no goalie fixes a team that gives up this many chances.

concerns.title: Opposing defensemen and centers feast
concerns.body: Opposing defensemen put up 0.52 points a game, well above their expected 0.3, which ranks 31st, and centers also beat their norms (29th). That points to loose coverage of activating defensemen and the middle of the ice. It fits the shot-share numbers, so expect it to persist.

trend.note: A dreadful early November, capped by a 2-9 loss at Carolina, gave way to a 3-1-1 run on a surge of goals. The underlying share numbers have barely moved through either stretch.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft defenses, two elite goaltending teams: a split is realistic
weekAhead.body:
The week opens in Seattle, the friendliest matchup on the schedule. The Kraken are 30th on the site, last in CF % at 0.42, and own the league's worst penalty kill at 60.7%, so Chicago's league-average power play should get chances to cash in. Home games against the Rangers and Wild follow, and both swing hard the other way. New York kills 90% of its penalties and has the league's best all-situations save %, while Minnesota (17-3-5) leads the league in Goalies GSAx at 16.2 and allows the fewest goals.

The week closes the night after Minnesota, in Winnipeg. The Jets give up the most shots on goal in the league at 31.6 a game and let opposing defensemen score more than anyone, so a tired Chicago team still has a real opening there. Two wins from the Seattle and Winnipeg games would be a good week. Anything against the Rangers or Wild would be a bonus against goaltending this good.

keyMatchups.title: Power play vs Seattle's broken kill
keyMatchups.body: Seattle kills only 60.7% of its penalties, last in the league. Chicago's power play has been mid-pack at 21.7%, so this is the clearest edge of the week. The Kraken's wingers also give up 0.95 points a game to opposing wingers, 30th.

keyMatchups.title: Finishing against elite goaltending
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota's goalies are +16.2 GSAx and New York's save % ranks 1st. Chicago's recent scoring burst came partly on improved finishing, and these two teams are where that gets tested. Expect the scoring to dry up for those two games.

keyMatchups.title: Winnipeg's porous shot suppression
keyMatchups.body: The Jets allow 31.6 shots on goal a game, 32nd. They also rank last against opposing defensemen, giving up 0.7 points a game. Even on the second night of a back-to-back, this is the game where Chicago's volume should finally look respectable.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts in goal on the Minnesota-Winnipeg back-to-back, since Soderblom's starts have been the worst of the season.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect Chicago to look a bit better on the scoreboard and about the same in the standings. The shooting and save percentages sit below league norms and should drift up, which will trim the -1.33 goal margin. The 5-on-5 shot and chance shares have held near the league's bottom for three seasons, though, and nothing in the sheet suggests they are about to break. The power play and penalty kill are close to average and should stay that way.

The current pace of 62 points looks like the middle of the realistic range. A modest bounce in save % gets the team into the mid-60s, short of last season's 72. Another bottom-three finish is the most likely outcome.
swingFactors: Knight's share of starts and his save %
Whether shooting % climbs toward league average

confidence.note: 24 games is a modest sample, but the shot-share profile matches the two prior seasons.
